text:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx spike observed for hosted API (route: /v1/*). automated threshold triggered at 18:07 UTC. severity: P1 :rotating_light:

josh: i'm oncall. looking at grafana now, seen a big jump in 502/504s starting ~18:05 UTC.

maya: stack traces show timeouts talking to auth-service and config-service. lots of downstream 504s from org-lookup.

rachel: paging SREs and infra. quick question: any recent deploys in the last 10m? deploy-bot: deploys: 
```
deploy-bot: 18:01 UTC — config-service v2.7.4 rolled to canary (50%)
deploy-bot: 17:52 UTC — auth-service hotfix v1.3.2 rolled to prod
```

lee: ugh, config-service canary aligns with start of spike. could be a bad code path increasing auth lookups.

josh: running a high-level impact check. on hosted: 8% of requests are returning 5xx in past 5m, errors concentrated on POST /v1/generate and auth token exchange endpoints.

maya: logs (sample):
```
[18:05:21] upstream auth-service timeout: context deadline exceeded
[18:05:22] org-lookup: request timeout after 5s
[18:05:23] gateway: 502 from auth-service
```

rachel: can we temporarily divert traffic to stable config-service and scale auth? options: rollback canary, scale auth replicas, bump timeouts, add circuit breaker.

josh: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale auth-service x2 2) reduce calling rate from API gateway (short-term token bucket) 3) disable non-critical config reads (feature flags) 4) start canary rollback if no improvement in 3m.

maya: executing scale now: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment auth-service --replicas=6` — will post result.

maya: auth pods are spinning up, readiness probes failing on pod-4 (OOMKilled) — looks like increased load + lower memory after recent image.

lee: are we sure it's config causing auth to amp? Could be a retry storm from gateway due to timeouts.

josh: good point. check gateway retry policy. rachel, can you push a temporary change to reduce retries from 3 -> 1 for the auth route?

rachel: applying change to gateway policy:
```
PATCH /gateway/route/auth
retries: 1
timeout: 6s
```
applied 18:11 UTC.

customer-success-bot: reviewing customer impact, sampling logs for major orgs — org-42, org-99 showing higher 5xx. CS notified for top 5 affected customers.

josh: after scaling and retry reduction, error rate dropped to 3.2% and p95 latency improved. still seeing occasional 502s.

maya: investigating OOMKilled on new auth pods. looks like auth image change reduced heap; creating a diagnostic pod to run heap dump.

lee: start rollback of config-service canary to stable (immediate) — `kubectl rollout undo deployment config-service --to-revision=152`

rachel: rollback started at 18:14 UTC. monitor shows canary traffic dropping.

incident-bot: NOTE — paging: primary oncall (josh) is handling, incident declared. creating incident channel.

josh: switching to incident channel #inc-1819992222 for root cause triage. leaving a short timeline here for audit.

maya: quick mitigation: we also toggled on a cache hit for org-lookup (30s TTL) at gateway layer to reduce downstream calls. patched at 18:15 UTC.

josh: customer impact update: approx 7.5k failed requests in last 10m, affecting hosted API only. no confirmed data exfiltration. CS reached out to impacted accounts with ETA.

rachel: post-rollback metrics look promising — error rate back to 0.9% after 18:20 UTC. auth pod OOMs stopped once new pods came up with corrected image (we reverted image config).

lee: probable root cause hypothesis: canary config introduced additional synchronous org lookups on generate path, increasing auth load and triggering retries/timeouts causing a cascading failure.

maya: follow-ups to list: 1) revert config change permanently until more testing 2) add circuit breaker + caching for org-lookup 3) increase alerting thresholds for auth latency to catch earlier 4) run load test for config changes against auth in staging 5) postmortem within 48h.

josh: assigning owners: rachel -> rollback + long-term fix; maya -> diagnostics & postmortem; lee -> alert windows & canary gating; josh -> incident writeup & customer comms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation successful, services recovered to normal SLOs at 18:24 UTC. please follow up in postmortem. :white_check_mark:

josh: adding immediate notes for postmortem: avoid sync org lookup on hot path, add fallback cache, tighten canary gating (traffic ramp and smoke checks), ensure memory limits match image changes.

maya: uploading diagnostic logs and heap dumps to S3 at s3://redwood-incident-logs/1819992222/ — link shared in incident channel.

rachel: closing on-call tasks; will coordinate with release owner to hold config change until patch validated.

josh: thanks team. will create the formal postmortem and link here. :pray:
